propositions.text: Bristol-Myers Squibb & Gilead Sciences, LLC and Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. appeal from the January 13, 2014 judgment of the Federal Court dismissing their application under s. 6 of the PMNOC Regulations.
propositions.quote: Bristol-Myers Squibb & Gilead Sciences, LLC and Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. (collectively, the appellants) appeal from the January 13, 2014 judgment of the Federal Court (2014 FC 30) dismissing their application made under s. 6 of the Patented Medicines (Notice of Compliance) Regulations, SOR/93-133 (PMNOC Regulations).

propositions.text: The appellants sought an order prohibiting the Minister of Health from issuing a Notice of Compliance to Teva Canada Limited for a generic version of Atripla.
propositions.quote: the appellants sought an order prohibiting the Minister of Health from issuing a Notice of Compliance to Teva Canada Limited for a generic version of the appellants’ combination anti-retroviral medicine marketed under the brand name Atripla.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants appeal the Federal Court's dismissal of their application to prohibit a Notice of Compliance for Teva's generic Atripla.

propositions.text: The appellants’ application responded to Teva's Notice of Allegation asserting non-infringement and invalidity of Patent 2,279,198.
propositions.quote: The appellants’ application was made in response to a Notice of Allegation (NOA) dated December 22, 2011, in which Teva asserted that its proposed product would not infringe Canadian Letters Patent 2,279,198, which is owned by Merck and licensed to the other appellants. Teva also alleged that the Patent is invalid.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants' application responded to Teva's Notice of Allegation claiming non-infringement and invalidity of the patent.

propositions.text: The Federal Court found the appellants failed to prove Teva tablets will infringe the Patent.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court found that the appellants had failed to prove on the balance of probabilities that the Teva tablets will infringe the Patent.

propositions.text: The Federal Court was not satisfied that the Teva tablets contain Form I efavirenz, the compound claimed in the Patent.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court was not satisfied that the Teva tablets contain Form I efavirenz, the compound claimed in the Patent.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court found the appellants did not prove Teva's tablets infringe or contain the patented compound.

propositions.text: The Federal Court found the appellants’ tests were not a reliable proxy for Teva’s manufacturing process.
propositions.quote: the appellants had failed to prove that the tests which they had conducted were a reliable proxy for the process Teva used to manufacture its tablets.

propositions.text: The Federal Court had concerns about differences in grinding force, lack of particulars, expert not observing tests, unnecessary heating, and missing excipients in the tests.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court had concerns about: the lack of correspondence between the grinding force applied in the appellants’ tests and the force exerted by Teva’s process; the lack of particulars on the grinding force applied in the tests; the failure of the appellants’ expert to observe the tests; the addition of unnecessary heating steps into the tests; and the failure to include excipients into the testing material.

propositions.text: The Federal Court generally preferred Teva’s expert evidence over the appellants’.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court generally preferred the evidence of Teva’s expert over that of the appellants.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court found the appellants' tests unreliable and preferred Teva's expert evidence due to several concerns with the appellants' methods.

propositions.text: Did the Federal Court apply the proper evidentiary standard?
propositions.quote: First, they submit that the Federal Court failed to apply the proper evidentiary standard.

propositions.text: Should the Federal Court have drawn an adverse inference against Teva for refusing to produce its tablets?
propositions.quote: Second, they submit that the Federal Court failed to draw an adverse inference against Teva for refusing to produce its tablets to the appellants for testing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants raise two issues: the evidentiary standard and whether an adverse inference should have been drawn against Teva.

propositions.text: This appeal raises questions of mixed fact and law, not extricable questions of law.
propositions.quote: this appeal does not raise extricable questions of law but, rather, questions of mixed fact and law suffused by fact, and questions of fact.

propositions.text: The appellants must demonstrate palpable and overriding error for appellate intervention.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the appellants must demonstrate palpable and overriding error

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appeal concerns mixed fact and law, requiring proof of palpable and overriding error for intervention.

propositions.text: The Federal Court made no palpable and overriding error in finding the appellants’ testing methods unreliable and not proving infringement.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court committed no palpable and overriding error in concluding that the appellants’ testing methods were not a reliable proxy for Teva’s manufacturing process, and that as such, the appellants had not proven that the Teva tablets infringe.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no palpable and overriding error in the Federal Court's conclusion about the unreliability of the appellants' testing methods.

propositions.text: The Federal Court judge applied the correct burden of proof, the balance of probabilities, and did not impose an impossible burden on the appellants.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court judge applied throughout the correct burden of proof, the balance of probabilities (at para. 20). The Judge’s approach did not impose on the appellants a burden that was impossible to meet.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Federal Court applied the correct burden of proof and did not impose an impossible standard on the appellants.

propositions.text: Appellants argued Teva had an initial burden to put its non-infringement allegations 'into play' before the appellants had to disprove them.
propositions.quote: counsel stressed that in applications brought under s. 6 of the PMNOC Regulations, the second person (Teva) has an initial burden to put its allegations “into play” by presenting evidence sufficient to give them an air of reality.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argued Teva had an initial evidentiary burden before the appellants had to disprove non-infringement allegations.

propositions.text: The appellants cited Pfizer v. Apotex to support their argument about Teva's initial evidentiary burden.
propositions.quote: In support of this argument, the appellants cited Pfizer Canada Inc. v. Apotex Inc., 2007 FC 26 at paragraphs 9, 12, [2007] F.C.J. No. 36 (QL), aff’d 2007 FCA 195, 367 N.R. 98.

propositions.text: The Pfizer case's requirement for the second person to put allegations 'into play' applies only to invalidity, not non-infringement.
propositions.quote: However, in that case, the Federal Court’s finding that the second person must present evidence putting their allegations “into play” relates solely to allegations of invalidity.

propositions.text: There is no presumption of validity or initial onus on Teva for non-infringement allegations in this case.
propositions.quote: However, in the case at bar, the allegation is non-infringement, not invalidity. There is no presumption in play and, thus, no initial onus on the second person to put forward evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants relied on Pfizer v. Apotex, but the court finds its evidentiary rule applies only to invalidity, not non-infringement.

propositions.text: Once Teva alleged non-infringement in its NOA, there was no further evidentiary burden on it; its allegation was 'in play.'
propositions.quote: there was no further evidentiary burden on it; its allegation of non-infringement was “in play.”

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Teva's non-infringement allegation was 'in play' with no further evidentiary burden after its NOA.

propositions.text: The court rejects the appellants’ submission that an adverse inference should have been drawn against Teva for not producing its tablets.
propositions.quote: I also reject the appellants’ submission that the Federal Court should have drawn an adverse inference against Teva for failing to produce its tablets.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the appellants' argument for an adverse inference against Teva for not producing tablets.

propositions.text: The Federal Court found the appellants were well-equipped to make the compound for testing and Teva undertook not to dispute the tested material's equivalence.
propositions.quote: the appellants were “better equipped than most” to make the compound for testing purposes and could have done so (footnote to para. 24). Also, Teva undertook not to assert that the material obtained and tested by the appellants was different in character or composition from Form Teva.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court found the appellants could make the compound for testing and Teva agreed not to dispute equivalence of tested material.

propositions.text: The Federal Court's decision not to draw an adverse inference is supported by the fact that production is not required under s. 6(7) of the PMNOC Regulations.
propositions.quote: the fact that production is not required under s. 6(7) of the PMNOC Regulations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Federal Court's refusal to draw an adverse inference is supported by the regulations not requiring production.

propositions.text: The appellants have not shown any palpable and overriding error by the Federal Court judge on this point.
propositions.quote: the appellants have failed to demonstrate any palpable and overriding error on the part of the Federal Court judge on this point.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellants have not shown any palpable and overriding error by the Federal Court judge.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed with costs.
propositions.quote: I would dismiss the appeal, with costs.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal with costs.
